issues.legal_issue: A Hindu widow’s mortgage of inherited property binds the reversioners only when supported by legal necessity or by a representation of necessity followed by bona fide inquiry.
material_facts: The widow executed a security bond over property inherited from her deceased son to secure a loan made to her other son.
The loan had already been obtained, and the security bond was executed to protect that son from threatened proceedings after property included in his mortgage was found not to belong to him.
The money deposited from the loan did not benefit the inherited estate, and the bond did not represent that it was executed to meet a necessity of that estate.
The courts found no legal necessity and no representation of necessity supported by bona fide inquiry.
issues.conclusion: The security bond was not binding on the reversioners and could operate only on the widow’s interest in the property.
issues.legal_principle: A Hindu widow has qualified proprietorship, and restrictions on her power to alienate are inseparable from that estate. She may convey an absolute title for legal necessity. Even if necessity did not actually exist, an alienation may bind the estate where necessity was represented and the alienee made bona fide inquiries and satisfied herself as far as reasonably possible. Otherwise, the alienee obtains only the widow’s interest. The Court relied on The Collector of Masulipatam v. Cavaly Venkata and Hunoomanpersaud Pandey v. Musammat Babooee Munraj Koonweree.

rule.if: widow_alienation_dispute and actual_necessity_absent and not (necessity_represented and bona_fide_inquiry_made)

predicates.widow_alienation_dispute: A reversioner challenges an alienation made by a widow of property inherited from a deceased family member.
predicates.actual_necessity_absent: The alienation was not made to meet an actual legal necessity of the inherited estate.
predicates.necessity_represented: The alienor or another person represented that a legal necessity existed for the alienation.
predicates.bona_fide_inquiry_made: The alienee made bona fide inquiries and satisfied herself as far as reasonably possible that the represented necessity existed.
predicates.alienee_gets_only_widow_estate: The alienee receives only the widow’s interest in the property, which does not bind the reversionary interest.

issues.definition: When a reversioner challenges a widow’s alienation, the alienee gets only the widow’s estate if actual necessity was absent and necessity was not both represented and investigated bona fide.

issues.legal_issue: A presumptive reversioner’s consent to a widow’s alienation raises a rebuttable presumption but does not prevent the actual reversioner from proving that the alienation lacked legal necessity and proper inquiry.
material_facts: The person who was the immediate presumptive reversioner joined the widow in executing the security bond.
The evidence established that there was no legal necessity and no proper bona fide inquiry by the mortgagee.
The courts found that the presumption arising from the presumptive reversioner’s consent had been rebutted.
issues.conclusion: The presumptive reversioner’s consent did not make the security bond binding on the actual reversioners.
issues.legal_principle: Consent by an immediate reversioner may raise a presumption that the alienation was for legal necessity or that the alienee made proper and bona fide inquiry, but that presumption is rebuttable. The actual reversioner may prove the absence of necessity and inquiry. The Court relied on Debi Prasad Chowdhury v. Golap Bhagat and Rangasami Gounden v. Nachiappa Gounden.

predicates.widow_alienation_dispute: A reversioner challenges an alienation made by a widow of inherited property.
predicates.presumptive_reversioner_joined: The person who was then the immediate presumptive reversioner joined in the widow’s alienation.
predicates.presumption_rebutted: Evidence established that the alienation lacked legal necessity and that the alienee had not made proper bona fide inquiry.
predicates.presumptive_reversioner_consent_does_not: The consent does not prevent the actual reversioner from challenging the alienation.

issues.definition: In a challenge to a widow’s alienation, consent by the presumptive reversioner does not bind the actual reversioner when the resulting presumption is rebutted.

issues.legal_issue: An eventual reversioner who claims through the last male holder rather than through a preceding presumptive reversioner is not bound by that preceding reversioner’s admission about the necessity for an alienation.
material_facts: A person who had become the immediate reversioner after the death of the earlier presumptive reversioner made a declaration that the widow’s debts were for legal necessity.
The claimants were that person’s sons, but they claimed as heirs of the deceased property holder, not through their father.
The declaration was not made to the purchasers involved in the challenged transactions.
issues.conclusion: The declaration did not bind the claimants.
issues.legal_principle: No person has a vested right while the widow is alive, and an eventual reversioner does not claim through a person who merely preceded that reversioner in the line of presumptive succession. The Court considered Rangasami Gounden v. Nachiappa Gounden, which explained the relevant passage in Bajrangi v. Manokarnika.

predicates.reversionary_title_claim_case: A claimant seeks property as an eventual reversioner after the widow’s interest ends.
predicates.prior_presumptive_reversioner_made_admis: A person who preceded the claimant as presumptive reversioner made an admission about the necessity for an alienation.
predicates.claimant_claims_through_last_male_holder: The claimant derives title from the last male holder rather than through the person who made the admission.
predicates.prior_reversioner_admission_does_not_bin: The prior presumptive reversioner’s admission does not bind the claimant.

issues.definition: In a reversionary title claim, an admission by a preceding presumptive reversioner does not bind a claimant who derives title from the last male holder instead of through that person.

issues.legal_issue: A subsequent purchaser cannot acquire a better title than the interest held by the purchaser at an earlier sale enforcing an alienation by a widow that did not bind the reversioners.
material_facts: The mortgagee obtained a decree enforcing the security bond, and the disputed property was sold in execution.
A purchaser at that sale later conveyed the property to another purchaser, who had provided value and claimed to have made inquiries and obtained legal advice.
The courts found no legal necessity for the security bond and no representation of necessity supported by bona fide inquiry.
issues.conclusion: The subsequent purchaser acquired only the widow’s interest, and the purchaser’s bona fides, payment of value, inquiries, and legal advice did not give him a higher title.
issues.legal_principle: A widow’s limited interest is not analogous to an equitable estate protected in the hands of a bona fide purchaser for value without notice. If an alienation does not bind the reversioners, a later transferee cannot obtain a greater interest than the earlier transferee held. The Court relied on The Collector of Masulipatam v. Cavaly Venkata and Hunoomanpersaud Pandey v. Musammat Babooee Munraj Koonweree.

predicates.downstream_purchaser_title_case: A purchaser claims property through a person who acquired it under an alienation made by a widow.
predicates.underlying_widow_alienation_not_binding_: The widow’s alienation did not bind the reversioners because legal necessity or the required represented necessity and bona fide inquiry were absent.
predicates.downstream_purchaser_gets_no_better_titl: The later purchaser acquires no greater interest than the widow’s interest that passed through the earlier transfer.

issues.definition: A purchaser claiming through an alienation that did not bind the reversioners receives no greater title than the widow’s interest.
